topic: Cracking the Code: Information Theory and Entropy in Wordle
target_audience: University students (CS or Data Science focus)

outline.topic: Cracking the Code: Information Theory and Entropy in Wordle
outline.target_audience: University students (CS or Data Science focus)

sections.title: The Intuition: What is Information?
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'surprise' as the core of information. Using binary trees, explain that information is the reduction of uncertainty. Prerequisite: Basic probability (P(x)).
sections.example: A 'Robot Detective' trying to find a cat hidden in one of 4 boxes. Each 'yes/no' question splits the search space in half, providing exactly 1 bit of information.

sections.title: Quantifying Uncertainty: The Entropy Formula
sections.content: Define Entropy (H) as the weighted average of information (surprises). Present the formula H(X) = -Σ P(x) log2 P(x) using a visual bar chart where the height represents probability and the width represents the 'surprise' value.
sections.example: Visualizing Wordle guess outcomes: A uniform distribution of outcomes (many possible words left) results in high entropy, while a skewed distribution (only 1-2 words left) results in low entropy.

sections.title: The Strategy: Maximizing Information Gain
sections.content: Explain that an optimal Wordle bot chooses a word that produces the most 'Expected Information Gain' (the greatest reduction in entropy). Show a transition animation where a 'bad' word shrinks the pool by 10% vs a 'good' word shrinking it by 90%.
sections.example: Comparing 'XYLID' (rare letters, low entropy) vs 'ARISE' (common letters, high entropy) against a pool of 2,300 words. 'ARISE' provides a much larger partition of the probability space.

sections.title: The Feedback Loop: Iterative Optimization
sections.content: Summarize the process: Guess -> Observe Pattern (Green/Yellow/Gray) -> Update Probability Distribution -> Repeat. Emphasize that entropy is dynamic—it decreases with every piece of feedback.
sections.example: A 'Cyber-Squirrel' algorithm: It narrows down a target word from 2,000 choices to 1 within 3-4 moves by prioritizing 'Maximum Entropy' guesses to prune the decision tree.
